lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the strategic question 'what is this fork for, now that upstream ships Marlin for Turing' has a complete evidence base: upstream merged the kernel and then froze it; upstream broke the sm75 attention surface and left the fix stalled; and the sibling fork has already demonstrated both divergence strategies on real hardware. (1) The merged upstream sm75 Marlin path: PR #29901 (Jinzhen Lin, Ant Group; merged 2025-12-16) plus #31000/#31008 (2025-12-19, compressed-tensors min capability 8.0->7.5), first released in v0.14.0 (2026-01-20). Verified at the fork pin (79378fe6e8 = v0.28.1rc0+23, 2026-08-27): marlin.cuh compiles every cp_async* helper below __CUDA_ARCH__ 800 into synchronous LDG->STS pointer copies with no-op commit/wait fences; marlin_mma.h carries six __CUDA_ARCH__==750 blocks with k16 split as two m16n8k8 issues; generate_kernels.py forces config_sm75['stages']=2 (vs 4 on Ampere); CMakeLists.txt has dedicated MARLIN_SM75_ARCHS/MARLIN_MOE_SM75_ARCHS blocks; Turing is the only architecture where use_fp16_accum can be true. Formats: GPTQ/AWQ W4A16, W4A8-INT8 activations (VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE=int8), W8A16-FP8 via MarlinFP8, NVFP4A16; MXFP4 excluded (needs BF16 activations Turing lacks). (2) Upstream evolution SINCE, none of it reworking the sm75 pipeline: #33076 NVFP4/FP8 weights on Turing (in v0.16.0, 2026-02-25, alongside a breaking 'Marlin 24 quantization' change and BitBlas removal); v0.19.0 (2026-04-03) Marlin-family fixes (AWQ Marlin on ROCm, an FP8 compressed-tensors fix, an NVFP4 NaN/Inf fix); #43731 (2026-05-27) TritonW4A16LinearKernel as CUDA fallback for non-Marlin-aligned shapes; #45176 (2026-06-11) torch stable-ABI move to csrc/libtorch_stable/; #45295/#45703 (2026-06-12/23) Marlin thread-tile padding dense then MoE; #45375 (2026-06-22) modelopt_mixed on Turing (riding with the FlashInfer floor raise); v0.26.0 (2026-07-27) bounded peak memory when repacking FP4 MoE weights for Marlin; v0.27.0 (2026-08-10) 'coalesced HBM access in the Marlin INT4-FP8 AWQ preprocess kernel' [uncertain: marlin_v0270_preprocess_sm75_scope - PR not individually identified; the repack/preprocess helpers are arch-agnostic so sm75 almost certainly rides along, but this was not confirmed]. Net: the two-stage sm75 substitution is untouched upstream for nine months (Dec 2025 -> Sep 2026), so the kernel the fork must beat is current and static. (3) The attention surface upstream broke: v0.23.0 (2026-06-15) is the last release where sm75 offered candidates ['FLASHINFER','TRITON_ATTN'] with fp8 KV; v0.24.0 (2026-06-29) raised the FlashInfer floor to SM80 (commit cf16db7, deliberate and temporary, citing flashinfer#3620/#3621) - regression #47549 (opened 2026-07-03, 18x RTX 8000 fleet, 2x KV-capacity loss, 5-10x decode collapse at 22K ctx) sits open with zero maintainer response, the revert PR #46943 has sat in draft since 2026-06-28, flashinfer's head_dim-256 smem fix #3526 merged 2026-07-22 but the head_dim-128 fix #3621 is still open, and the floor is still SM80 on main as of 2026-09-07. No release from v0.22.0 through v0.28.0 mentions Turing/sm75 in its notes (verified on the releases pages this run); upstream's kernel investment is SM90/SM100/SM12x/GB10-class. (4) The engine underneath moved twice: async scheduling default since v0.14.0; Model Runner V2 (blog 2026-03-24, opt-in VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 in the v0.18.0 era; persistent batching, GPU-native Triton input prep, Triton-native sampler) became default for all dense models in v0.25.0 (#44443, 2026-07-11) and default for all models via #53183 by the v0.28 era (carried in the fork's pin; Q3-2026 roadmap #48168 deprecates MRV1); v0.25.0 also removed PagedAttention (#47361). MRV2's GPU-native prep and sampler are Triton, i.e. FMA-floor-exposed on sm75 (Triton >=3.3 emits no tensor-core math on sm75) - no compute-capability constraint is documented in the blog, and it demonstrably serves on Turing (see (5)), but its sm75 cost is unmeasured here [uncertain: weicj_v02_mrv2_mode; fork_27b_gate_mrv2_active - whether the fork's Qwen3.6-27B (75% GDN hybrid) gate ran under MRV2 or fell back to MRV1 is not recorded]. (5) The sibling fork, both strategies demonstrated: weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive (created 2026-06-02, 815 stars / 123 forks / 12 open issues / 10 PRs). Its v0.1.x line (final v0.1.17, 2026-08-24, 'substituted by 0.2.x') is the STRAND-THEN-DIVERGE strategy: base vLLM 0.21.0, CUDA 12.8, torch 2.11, dual 22GB 2080 Ti + NVLink TP=2, 100+ tok/s single-request decode on Qwen3.6-27B FP8 with MTP3. Its v0.2.x line (v0.2.1-pre 2026-08-16, -pre2 2026-08-21, -pre3 2026-08-27) is the REBASE-PLUS-PATCHES strategy: 'SM75 migration' onto upstream vLLM v0.27.1 (the post-v0.24, MRV2-default-for-dense, CUDA-13 generation; CUDA 13.0 / PyTorch 2.13 / Python 3.12), validated non-eager TP=2/PP=1 CUDA-graph serving at 1570.57/30.01 prefill/decode tok/s (4K/128, FP16 KV) and 1522.72/75.83 with MTP3, Qwen3.8-27B FP8/NVFP4/INT8-W8A8/AWQ-INT4 profiles validated, Gemma4 baseline/experimental, MXFP4 explicitly unsupported on SM75 Marlin kernels, and - critically - vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py locally holding supports_compute_capability at >= (7,5) with an in-code comment: upstream 'temporarily raises this floor' (flashinfer#3620), 'This fork retains SM75 for its validated Turing route', unsupported combinations 'still fail their individual combination checks' - i.e. the entire attention divergence from current upstream is one capability constant plus per-combination checks, proven on real dual-Turing hardware. Its stated policy: 'will not strictly follow upstream vLLM', incoming patches 're-validated within the SM75-specific scope'; no upstreaming statements. It carries Marlin (dense + MoE weight routes), FlashInfer attention + sampling, FlashQLA-SM70-SM75 (GDN prefill, packed-varlen added in -pre3), TurboQuant K8V4 + INT8 KV, MTP3, CUDAGraph-first runtime - no GEMM TFLOP/s microbenchmarks published, so kernel-level comparison must be run, not read. (6) Fresh upstream correctness drift inside the fork's own fastest lane: issue #48905 (opened 2026-07-17, still open, fix PR #48926 open) - Marlin W4A8 with int8 activations silently corrupts when weight group scales are negative (helper packs signed int16, kernel reads unsigned; median relative error 0.008 -> 16.4, no error raised); AutoRound symmetric-int4 checkpoints legitimately emit ~50% negative scales while GPTQ/AWQ/llm-compressor emit positive-only. Tested on a 3090 but the path is arch-agnostic, so sm75 W4A8-int8 on AutoRound checkpoints is exposed upstream today - and AutoRound is this fork's plan/0005 stage-4 lane.
lacuna.sm75_viability: What actually runs on Turing-class hardware today, per kernel class, with the fork's position measured against both competitors. DENSE GEMM (W4A16/W4A8/W8A16-FP8/NVFP4A16 Marlin): upstream sm75 Marlin runs on this host's 2x Quadro RTX 6000 (locked 1455 MHz) at 51-57 TFLOP/s at M512 across model shapes (N4096/K4096, N11008/K4096, N4096/K11008), float64-checked, weight-bound ~0.60 TFLOP/s at M1 (MEMORY 2026-08-28). The fork's validated kernels (opt1 fp16-staged, opt2 register-dequant, pipe, regdeq dispatch-table winner regdeq_64_128_64_w4x2 nz=2, kshard2 fp32-partials) pass the float64 oracle everywhere; recorded sweep (kernel-search.md, 2026-08-28): fork best-per-regime 0.24/1.85/6.72/17.48/23.49 TFLOP/s across M 1/8/32/128/512 vs incumbent 0.60/4.86/13.98/35.13/51.38 - the M>=128 regime fails acceptance worst-case 2.2x (23.49 vs 51.38); the fork's one recorded win over the incumbent is cross-GPU: kshard2 fp32 partials over NVLink at 1.68x (M=64) and 1.36x (M=512) [uncertain: fork_decode_regime_winner - the w4a16 sibling's prose and this item's brief characterize the fork as 'already winning all decode regimes M 1-32', but both the MEMORY 2026-08-28 sweep table and the sibling's own numbers (fork 0.16-4.79 vs incumbent 0.60-13.98 at M 1-32) show the incumbent ahead single-GPU at every measured M; the discrepancy is unresolved in host records and the A/B probe below must settle it before any external differentiator claim]. Upstream's own 2080 Ti numbers (PR #29901): Marlin-Turing 2-3.3x over torch-fp16 at m=1 (0.0097-0.0115 vs 0.0320 ms, n2048-4096/k4096), w4a8-int8 the fastest config, trailing exllama-v2 at m>8 (exllama switches to dequant+cuBLAS) - the fork's benchmark-reconciliation target. MOE GEMM: upstream Marlin MoE on sm75 from #29901 + NVFP4 Marlin MoE #30881 (v0.14.0) + thread-tile padding #45703 + v0.26.0 repack peak-memory bound; community evidence it loads and serves (weicj 35B MoE routes at 256K text / 178K MTP3 context; T4 Qwen3-Next-80B AWQ loads via Marlin MoE but fails later on the separate BF16 torch.compile limitation); open crash surface #35922 (compressed-tensors MoE) and #38022 (Marlin MoE x MXFP4 gpt-oss). The fork's MoE grouped forward is plan/0002-validated but untuned (sibling item moe-kernels-sm75 owns the acceptance surface). ATTENTION: the only upstream sm75 candidate post-v0.24.0 is TRITON_ATTN (no quantized KV, 64 KB smem ceiling at head_dim>128); the viable sm75 attention assets are fork-only or sibling-fork-only - FlashInfer-sm75 (2x KV capacity via fp8 KV, restore = one capability constant), this fork's BRIDGE_ATTN (owns d256 for the 27B's full-attention layers), weicj's FlashQLA-SM70-SM75 (GDN prefill, packed-varlen) and TurboQuant K8V4 KV. ENGINE: the fork's retained Turing engine serves Qwen3.6-27B-AutoRound W4A16 TP=2 with all 14 gates passing (2026-09-06, PPL 2k 6.7761) on the v0.28.1rc0+23 pin; weicj proves the same class of stack on the current upstream generation (v0.27.1, CUDA 13, CUDA-graph TP=2, MTP3). Capability floors that shape every kernel-class decision (all measured on this host): no cp.async below sm80 (the incumbent's LDG->STS stages=2 substitution IS the pipelining deficit the plan/0004 campaign attacks); no sanctioned INT4 MMA (ptxas rejects .s4; register dequant permanent); k16 requires two k8 issues (m16n8k16 f32-acc is sm80); no BF16 (MXFP4 excluded - confirmed independently by weicj's release note 'MXFP4 unsupported on SM75 Marlin kernels'); FP16 tensor ceiling 101.7 TFLOP/s at 1455 MHz; occupancy legality gate >=2 resident blocks (one block caps at 43.8 TFLOP/s); W4A16 crossover M*~47 below which weight bytes, not tensor pipes, are the lever. Fallback semantics to keep loud: #43731 routes non-Marlin-aligned W4A16 shapes to TritonW4A16 (mma.884/FMA on sm75); post-v0.24 fall-through to TRITON_ATTN silently drops quantized KV; Marlin W4A8-int8 silently corrupts on negative scales (#48905) - three distinct silent-degradation paths, each needing an explicit assertion in the fork's gates.

effort_value.effort_estimate: A strategy-and-ledger item, not a kernel campaign (plan/0002/0004 own the kernels; sibling items own the engine rows). Deliverables: (1) commit this per-release ledger + the rebase-vs-diverge verdicts into the plan records (plan/0005 stage-11 amendment or a new plan/0005 appendix), half a session; (2) codify the standing sm75 patch set in the fork - the FlashInfer (7,5) floor constant (weicj's v0.2.x flashinfer.py diff is the exact reference) plus candidate-list and kv-dtype assertion tests that run per rebase - one session given the fork's test harness exists; (3) the A/B engine-base probe (current-pin-plus-constant vs v0.23.0 tag) about one day on the existing TU102 host, reusing the plan/0007 gate scripts; (4) the PR #29901 benchmark-table reconciliation on this host (already named in the w4a16 sibling's probe - shared, not duplicated). Rough size: 2-3 sessions total; zero new infrastructure.
effort_value.unlocks: A durable rebase policy that stops the drift class that bit v0.24.0 (silent candidate-list shrinkage caught only by assertion tests); freedom to move the engine base past v0.23.0 to current main without losing FlashInfer/fp8-KV - unlocking FlashInfer-era fixes (0.6.14+, XQA-class work where applicable) and MRV2 maturation for the both-card target (plan/0005 stage 13); the externally defensible differentiator statement ('beats upstream sm75 Marlin at decode regimes / matches weicj engine-level targets') with its evidence base settled; the template for absorbing weicj v0.2.x techniques (TurboQuant K8V4 handling, FlashQLA prefill, MTP3 routing) as cherry-picks instead of re-derivations; and the W4A8 negative-scale guard (#48905) that protects the fork's AutoRound lane from silent corruption.
effort_value.dependency_order: Nothing must land first - all evidence is in hand and the ledger can be committed immediately. Repo-internal: independent of the plan/0002/0004 kernel campaign (parallel-safe); feeds turing-engine-upstream-drift (shared ledger rows, its effort item 2 is exactly the assertion tests named here), both-card-tp-nvlink-serving (the engine-base choice this item makes is the base stage 13 benchmarks on), and w4a16-perf-acceptance (shares the PR #29901 table reconciliation; the fork_decode_regime_winner discrepancy must be settled before that item's differentiator claims go external). External prerequisites: none for the policy; the A/B probe needs the v0.23.0 container tag (public) and the fork's existing pinned FlashInfer build; absorbing weicj techniques later needs their v0.2.x branch (public). Parallelizable: everything except that the verdicts should be recorded before the next pin advance (the fork's pin discipline already gates this via software/--check).
effort_value.risk_notes: Per-class rebase risk, measured: dense GEMM - low (static nine months; the only absorbed churn was file moves and padding semantics, and #48905 is the one open correctness landmine, mitigated by an oracle case with negative scales); MoE - medium (active upstream churn #45703/v0.26.0/v0.27.0 plus open crash reports #35922/#38022 - rebasing buys fixes, diverging buys none); attention - the defining risk, proven twice (V0/xformers removal, v0.24.0 floor raise shipped silently inside a Turing-friendly PR #45375), and the restore is stalled upstream (#46943 draft since 2026-06-28, flashinfer #3621 open), so the fork's one-constant patch is load-bearing indefinitely. MRV2 risk: the GPU-native Triton input prep and sampler sit on the sm75 FMA floor - serving is proven (weicj on v0.27.1; this fork's 27B gate on the v0.28.1rc0+23 pin) but the per-step cost is unmeasured, and MRV1 deprecation (#48168) means there is no long-term fallback to not engaging with it. Divergence risk: the 'beat upstream sm75 Marlin' claim is only current while the pin tracks current upstream - the claim ages with the pin; and the real competitive surface is weicj (v0.2.x moving weekly through Aug 2026), not upstream (static). Numerics: upstream's fp16-accum-on-Turing rationale (halved FP32-acc MMA throughput) contradicts this host's TU102 microbench (f32-acc == f16-acc at ~101 TFLOP/s) [uncertain: upstream_marlin_fp16_accum_halving_claim - unverified here, plausibly a register-pressure effect]; tile-padding (#45295/#45703) silently changes shape dispatch on rebase; the v0.19.0 NVFP4 NaN/Inf fix must ride along if the fork serves NVFP4A16. Silent-fallback surface (three paths): TritonW4A16 routing for non-aligned shapes (#43731), TRITON_ATTN fall-through dropping quantized KV post-v0.24, and W4A8 negative-scale corruption (#48905) - each needs a loud assertion, not a benchmark. Benchmark validity: PR #29901's 2080 Ti tables and weicj's tok/s come from different clocks/stacks (CUDA 12.8 vs this host's 13.3) - cross-comparisons must be re-based onto the locked-clock protocol before any external claim.
effort_value.determinism_class: The mechanisms are inherited and stable per configuration (sibling verdicts): GEMM main loops bitwise per config (fixed traversal, no atomics outside split-K); split-K epilogues split into the fixed-order locks class (bitwise) vs use_atomic_add (statistical); attention-backend identity moves outputs at fp16-roundoff scale, so backend swaps are statistical-class and never bitwise-comparable. What THIS item adds is the rebase-decision discipline as a determinism contract: every upstream-base bump changes kernel selection surfaces (Marlin tile-padding dispatch, Triton codegen version, FlashInfer autotune caches, MRV2 prep kernels), so each ledger advance must re-attest the standing numeric anchors - PPL 2k in the 6.7761 +/- 0.0002 band, distinct3 logprob envelopes per context bucket, 2x float64-oracle passes on the kernel set (including asymmetric-weight and negative-scale cases), and recorded candidate lists + engaged kv-dtype strings in every serving transcript - before any timing is believed. The fork's decode-regime comparisons against the incumbent must additionally be single-config, fixed-dispatch-row runs (the dispatch table selects per shape; a rebase that shifts the table shifts the comparison object), and the median-of-N + cross-restart-median discipline (plan/0007) applies to any engine-level A/B between bases.

decision.priority_signal: VERDICT per kernel class. Dense GEMM: REBASE - upstream's sm75 Marlin is static, the fork's differentiator is its own kernel family behind the dispatch table, and the comparison target stays honest only while the pin tracks current upstream; there is nothing to gain from diverging the integration. MoE GEMM: REBASE and absorb - Marlin-MoE churn is upstream-active (padding, repack-memory, preprocess fixes) and rebuilding it fights churn for zero differentiator; the fork's value is tuning, not re-implementation. Attention: DIVERGE with the smallest loud patch set - one capability constant plus per-combination checks plus candidate assertions, exactly the weicj v0.2.x pattern proven on v0.27.1 hardware; upstream has no working quantized-KV sm75 path, the restore is stalled, and this fork additionally owns BRIDGE_ATTN (d256), which has no upstream counterpart at all. Per base: do NOT strand on v0.23.0 - the fork's pin is already at v0.28.1rc0+23 with the 27B gate green, and the v0.23.0-vs-current question reduces to whether the one-constant patch holds (weicj says yes on v0.27.1; the fork should verify on its own pin). FOR doing this item now: it is nearly free (2-3 sessions), it settles the differentiator narrative every other external claim leans on, it produces the assertion tests that are the only durable defense against the proven silent-drift class, and the fork_decode_regime_winner discrepancy must be resolved before the w4a16 acceptance campaign publishes anything. AGAINST: the kernel campaign (M>=128) is the bigger lever and is owned elsewhere; upstream is not racing (nine months static), so nothing forces this quarter; and the weicj fork already published the migration template, so the fork could free-ride its approach later - though that argument weakens as the fork's own pin ages. Window-closing: low from upstream, medium from weicj (its v0.2.x line is absorbing the same technique space - TurboQuant, FlashQLA, MTP3 - week by week, and first-mover validation data matters for the fork's reason-to-exist). Net: land the ledger + verdicts + assertion tests now as a maintenance row, sequence the A/B probe alongside the next kernel session.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0, oracle-first, no timing until numerics pass, one day on the existing TU102 host: (1) In the current pin worktree (79378fe6e8), apply the one-constant FlashInfer floor revert (7,5) - reference diff: weicj v0.2.x vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py - boot Qwen3.6-27B-AutoRound TP=2; assert candidates == ['FLASHINFER','TRITON_ATTN'] and that --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 is accepted at startup; oracle-check decode outputs against the float64 reference and hold PPL 2k in the 6.7761 +/- 0.0002 band; this settles 'current-pin-plus-one-constant' as a FlashInfer-capable engine base. (2) Same assertions against vllm-openai:v0.23.0 (Docker) on the same prompts - the pair of runs empirically validates the ledger's two attention rows (v0.23.0 last-zero-patch vs current-plus-constant) and their numeric equivalence band. (3) Incumbent-stability check: run the existing float64-checked marlin_bench at the three model shapes on both bases - if 51-57 TFLOP/s at M512 reproduces identically, the dense kernel surface is confirmed base-invariant and the dense-class 'rebase freely' verdict is proven, not asserted; while there, add the #48905 adversarial case (a synthetic W4A8 checkpoint with ~50% negative group scales) to the oracle set and record whether the fork's own kernels handle negative scales correctly.
